name: NOCD
short_description: The leading virtual OCD treatment platform connecting patients with ERP-trained therapists, offering specialized exposure and response prevention therapy covered by major insurance plans.
long_description: NOCD is the nation's largest provider of virtual therapy for Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder, founded in 2018 by Stephen Smith who struggled to find accessible OCD treatment himself. Headquartered in Chicago, Illinois, NOCD has raised over $90 million in funding and employs more than 500 licensed therapists specializing in Exposure and Response Prevention (ERP), the gold-standard treatment for OCD. The platform offers video-based therapy sessions complemented by a mobile app that provides between-session support, including tools for tracking exposures and messaging therapists. NOCD accepts most major insurance plans including Aetna, Cigna, Optum/UnitedHealthcare, and various Blue Cross Blue Shield plans, making specialized OCD treatment accessible and affordable. For therapists, NOCD provides comprehensive ERP training, handles all credentialing and billing, and offers competitive W-2 employment with benefits. The company has treated over 100,000 patients and has partnerships with many health systems and employers seeking to offer OCD treatment as part of their mental health benefits.

faqs.q: How much do NOCD therapists get paid?
faqs.a: NOCD therapists are W-2 employees with base salaries typically ranging from $65,000-95,000 depending on experience and location. Full-time employees receive comprehensive benefits including health insurance, dental, vision, 401k with match, and paid time off. NOCD handles all billing and credentialing.

faqs.q: Do I need ERP experience to work at NOCD?
faqs.a: No, ERP experience is preferred but not required. NOCD provides comprehensive Exposure and Response Prevention training to all therapists, along with ongoing supervision and professional development. You need to be fully licensed (LCSW, LMFT, LPC, PsyD, PhD, or equivalent).

NOCD accepts most major insurance plans including Aetna, Cigna, UnitedHealthcare/Optum, various Blue Cross Blue Shield plans, and Anthem. Patient copays typically range from $0-60 depending on their specific plan. Self-pay options are available for uninsured patients.

faqs.q: Is NOCD therapy effective for OCD?
faqs.a: NOCD specializes in Exposure and Response Prevention (ERP), which is considered the gold-standard, evidence-based treatment for OCD. Research shows ERP is effective for approximately 80% of people with OCD. NOCD's platform also includes between-session support through their mobile app to enhance treatment outcomes.
